title: Token reorder and quantization drift after prefill->decode batching transition
creator: Maya Chen
description: After landing the adaptive batching heuristic that moves select requests from prefill to the decode fast-path earlier in the pipeline, we observed intermittent correctness regressions in generation results: token reordering, occasional duplicated tokens, and small but growing numerical divergence in logits when using int8 quantized kernels on A100/GPU fleets. This ticket tracks investigation, repro, mitigation, and rollout plan.
observed_behavior: Reproduction on internal perf harness: ~1-2% of sampled requests show token order changes vs baseline (golden) decode path.
Numerical drift: per-token logit differences grow over decode steps, reaching ~1e-2 logit delta in worst cases for int8 kernels vs fp16 baseline.
Intermittent KV index mismatch logged in a small subset of runs: per-shard KV slot referenced an older prefix leading to token duplication.
Issue spikes when request sequence-length distribution has a high variance and adaptive-batcher switches route mid-prefill.
Failure surface correlated with fused-attention kernel preference flag enabled and cheap prefetch enabled in shard scheduler.
expected_behavior: Adaptive batching should preserve deterministic token ordering and numeric parity (within quantization bounds) with the canonical prefill->decode handoff. No KV slot misindexing or token duplication should occur.
reproduction_steps: Checkout branch: runtime/adaptive-routing-v2 and runtime/quant-int8-experiment (internal harness changes applied).
Launch perf harness using model: open-llm-2.1 with int8 quantization profile on a 2-shard A100 allocation.
Seed workload: mixed sequence lengths (50% short <64, 30% medium 64-512, 20% long 512-2048) with interleaved prefill-heavy and single-token decode requests.
Compare generated tokens and per-step logits against baseline run with adaptive batching disabled. Collect traces and KV index logs.
Observed divergences will appear within 10-60 decode steps in the non-deterministic runs.
investigation_notes: 03-03: Initial triage — confirmed it's regression introduced after adaptive-routing-v2 merge (rolled back reproduces baseline).

03-04: Added additional logging around KV slot allocation and per-request routing decision timestamps. Found cases where decoder started consuming a KV slab with stale base_offset when prefill had completed on different kernel variant.
03-05: Reproduced on single-GPU with sequence-shard shim by forcing route-switch; observed subtle off-by-one in slot_write_index calculation when prefetch path executed concurrently.

03-06: Observed increased floating-point drift when using int8 kernel: quant-dequant rounding amplifies token-choice differences after misaligned KV read windows. fp16 baseline remains stable, suggesting two causes (indexing race + quant noise).

03-08: Stress tests against batch-coalescer show that the coalescer may reorder request window boundaries under load; timing interaction with kernel selection leads to misaligned KV write/read boundaries.
03-10: Memory fence added in debug build eliminated reproducible misindex in local runs but has measurable perf regression (~3% p50).
hypothesis: A race between adaptive batcher route-switch (prefetch + prefill) and kernel selection causes KV write/read boundary misalignment. When the int8 fused-attention kernel is chosen mid-prefill, its prefetch path writes KV slots with different alignment semantics. The decode path occasionally reads from a misaligned base_offset resulting in token duplication and amplified by quantization rounding, producing numerical drift.
mitigation: Short-term: disable PREFETCH_ON_ROUTE_SWITCH and fallback to conservative kernel selection for mixed-length requests (feature flag guarded) — this eliminates the race at the cost of a modest latency increase for affected cases. Added a canary flag for high-variance workloads.
next_steps: (A) Implement deterministic KV slot fencing: ensure atomic commit of base_offset after any prefetch-write and require decode to validate fence token before reading.
(B) Add unit/integration tests that simulate route-switching to catch KV boundary races (deterministic harness).
(C) Add a lightweight verification step in runtime: per-request sequence-hash validation at handoff to detect misaligned windows in prod telemetry.
(D) Evaluate tighter quantization error tolerances and add post-quantization calibration for fused-attn kernels to reduce drift amplification.
(E) Plan rollout: enable fence+tests in canary region -> monitor token-order regressions and log rate -> widen rollout if green.
blockers: Need kernel maintainers to review proposed KV fencing approach for perf impact and correctness trade-offs (cc: kernel-team).
QA harness needs an update to run deterministic route-switch scenarios in the infra lab (infra-ticket pending).
